MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, JUNE 3, 2024

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR ROMANELLI at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Romanelli, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Schachter, Yoo

  Commissioners Absent:  Olson, Medawar

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

  Also Present: Steve Mckewen, City Attorney

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MAY 21, 2024

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 21, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

B.  BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS requested that more detail is added for cases that are resolved and
asked for the number of days that a case has been opened. Director Naughton stated that cases
that are closed are generally closed because they are brought into compliance; however, details
clarifying actions taken to resolve cases can be added.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired about cases that are referred to the prosecutor’s
office. Director Naughton stated that these cases are handled by the City Attorney’s Office.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS
to,
  APPROVE THE CONSENT CALENDAR

AYES: ROMANELLI, NICKLAS, REPP-LOADSMAN, SCHACHTER, YOO

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JUNE 3, 2024
  1
 7.  PUBLIC HEARING

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE

Director Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff report with an overview of the
zoning code updates that have been worked on thus far. The priority has been the commercial
district, which is where most changes to the City’s General Plan land use can be found. Director
Naughton provided an explanation of the current zoning and overlays in the commercial district
and how these were combined in order to create the new zoning districts in order to implement
the intent of the general plan. The new zoning districts include the Commercial General Mixed-
Use (CGMU) with 30 dwelling units per acre and the Commercial Limited Mixed-Use (CLMU) with
22 dwelling units per acre; an explanation with examples were provided for each.

Director Naughton stated that there were specific development standards created for uses and if
these standards are met, then they are permitted by right. She stated that the vision for height in
the commercial district was for three to four stories, however there was discussion regarding the
height of the Promenade where it may be appropriate to have five stories. She suggested that the
Planning Commission may want to consider adding some language in the ordinance to allow an
additional story or up to 60 feet with a CUP.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN commented that if a project were entirely commercial then
an additional floor may be appropriate. However, if a project is residential, would the developer
be able to apply through the City’s benefit density program. Director Naughton stated that yes,
they could, but the project would be required to incorporate specific community benefits to quality.
An alternative track would be to allow residential or residential mixed-use to apply for an additional
floor by a CUP process. Alternatively, it could be allowed for commercial only.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN agreed that she could see that it would be appropriate for
commercial only since residential/residential-mixed use already has a pathway to apply for an
additional floor (by way of the commercial density program).

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that as the
ordinance is written now, a Variance is the only pathway available to go above 50 feet in height.
After a brief discussion, Director Naughton suggested that the language included could be written
as any non-residential project greater than 50 feet and less than or equal to 60 feet or five stories
requires a CUP. The Planning Commission agreed.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about the height of the Promenade. Director Naughton
stated that it is approximately 90 feet. The project was approved through a series of entitlements
in the late 70’s.

Director Naughton provided an explanation and illustrations for the differences between CGMU
and CLMU. The maximum lot coverage in the CLMU is 35%, but it is meant to be a transition
zone between single-family residential to mixed-use. The development procedures for the CGMU
and CLMU were provided.

Director Naughton provided the current and the proposed zoning map and pointed out the areas
that will be affected by this update.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired about the additional requirements imposed by the
Landmark Overlay. Director Naughton stated that the Landmark Overlay requires that any
structures or characteristics of the site that initially were the reason for it being designated as such
be retained. Kelly’s Korner and the General Store would need to be retained intact if there were
any additional development there. Any activity on the site or the building requires Planning
Commission review.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN commented that a residential developer could buy this
property and then choose to use the State’s density bonus law program and propose 33 units per
acre, which means that they would have to raze everything on the property. Director Naughton
stated that staff would not be supportive of removing any structures and any development would
need to plan around them.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN further explained that a developer could claim a hardship
to meet the density and meet the objectives of the affordable housing plan; the City would be
challenged to determine if the landmark designation is appropriate. She further commented that
the current buildings are legal non-conforming under single-family designation and there is no
incentive to change them since the density is so low.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JUNE 3, 2024
  2
 Director Naughton stated that 13 Pepper Tree Lane was previously designated as Commercial
Limited. There is one existing commercial condo that fronts Hawthorne Blvd. and has been utilized
as a law office since the project was constructed in 2002, and the office space has been vacant
off and on. Changing the land use designation to Residential Planned Development (RPD), the
commercial condo would be legal non-conforming. If the office ceases to operate for more than a
year, the homeowners association could then utilize that condo space for a community center or
clubhouse or the use that they deem appropriate.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that the
commercial space is very small, if the HOA proposed to convert it to a single-family residential
unit, there it would require some type of entitlement modification.

Director Naughton stated that the site on Crenshaw Blvd. just north of Silver Spur was developed
a few years ago for a CalWater pump station as part of the PV Water Reliability Project. The
current zoning is RA-20,000 and the new zoning designation be Commercial Recreation.

Director Naughton stated that Levitt Park, which is at the corner of Crenshaw Blvd. and Silver
Spur Road was donated to the City and will change from Commercial General Mixed-Use to Open
Space.

Director Naughton stated that the sites identified for a new Institutional Workforce Housing
Overlay are Peninsula High School, Dapplegray Elementary School and Rolling Hills Covenant
Church. This will allow these property owners, if they so choose, to develop very low density (one
to two dwelling units to the acre) and a small section of their site for staff housing. She further
noted that there have been a number of state laws that have passed which gave institutional sites,
religious institutions and non-public higher education institutions the right to do much more intense
residential development than our overlay would allow. The general plan identified these sites and
it is another tool that property owners can use if they choose, and would require a CUP. Director
Naughton stated that due to concerns about this, staff had discussions with school district staff
last week and provided them assurance that this is not a mandate.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about the two properties owned by Rolling Hills Covenant
Church and it two dwelling units per acre would apply separately. Director Naughton stated that
she believes the general plan envisioned this being more appropriate for the larger site on the
south side of Palos Verdes Drive North. This would not allow for complete redevelopment of the
site and parking requirements would still need to be met for the uses that are on the site.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired about the State law regarding religious institutions
that she believes may allow for the removal of some parking. Director Naughton stated that she
does not know about parking, but there are affordability requirements.

CHAIR ROMANELLI inquired about the institutions that were not designated in this overlay.
Director Naughton stated that these properties were discussed during the General Plan Advisory
Committee meetings, and it was during those discussions that it was determined that these sites
were of sufficient size to support some small-scale residential development.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton stated that any
school district or religious institution property that is not in this overlay could take advantage of
what it available by State law.

Director Naughton stated that there was general cleanup needed. Chapters 17.24, CO and CL
Districts; 17.32 Scientific and Research District; 17.34 Quarry District are proposed to be
removed. Chapter 17.37 Mixed Use has been transferred to the CGMU and CLMU along with the
updated development standards. The City Attorney found outdated language in Chapter 17.58
Precise Plan of Design, and minor cleanup of the language, but no substantive policy related
changes were made in this chapter.

Director Naughton stated that the environmental findings were provided in the staff report and
stated that staff is relying on the General Plan EIR and Statement of Overriding Considerations
that were adopted along with the general plan.

Director Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open the public
hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues related to the zoning text amendment and the
amendments to the City’s zoning map, close the public hearing and adopt Resolution No. PA-
230037 recommending to the City Council the adoption of amendments to the Rolling Hills States
Municipal Code pertaining to Title 17 to conform with the City's 2040 General Plan and the
rezoning of certain properties and determining the code amendments and property rezonings are
exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JUNE 3, 2024
  3
 COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the commission can adopt this resolution even though
the objective design standards are still pending. Director Naughton stated that the plan is for the
objective design standards to be adopted by resolution. Staff has most of the text drafted to mimic
and mirror what is outlined in the basic development standards in the code sections, there are
final illustrations pending. The draft objective design standards will be coming before the Planning
Commission for review shortly after these amendments are adopted.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton explained the
new procedural track for the administrative use permit process. If the decision is appealed it would
come before the Planning Commission for a discretionary review.

COMMISISONER NICKLAS inquired about the institutional overlay and governs converting
existing building residential units. Director Naughton stated that it would still fall under the same
parameter; this only allows for residential use to be allowed on the site. The specifics will be
brought to the Planning Commission to discuss.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER YOO, Director Naughton stated that it would not
be beneficial for a commercial property to become a religious institution since it would be more
valuable to develop it as commercial or residential than a religious institution.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired about current and pending applications that are
in the Commercial General area. Director Naughton stated that there is one application for 90
residential units on two-acre site in the Peninsula Shopping Center and a preliminary application
for the approximately 10-acre site on Deep Valley Drive and Indian Peak for approximately 400-
unit mixed-use project. Status on both was provided.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN commented that under senior or residential care types
uses is Merrill Gardens, and asked if there are others under this category. Director Naughton
stated that Peninsula Pointe on Hawthorne Blvd. and Ravensburg recently received their
certificate of occupancy at the end of 2023. Director Naughton further stated that there is a
locational standard in the zoning ordinance of 1500 feet, that essentially means that as currently
written in the code, there is not opportunity for additional assisted living facilities in the commercial
district. The Planning Commission may want to take a look at this if there is any concern.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the law changes (hypothetically) on July 1, what time
frame of the applicant’s process does the old law or the new law apply. City Attorney McKewen
stated that he would need to look at the project since it depends on the circumstances, but
typically it is when a project has been approved.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-
LOADSMAN to,

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

No members of the public were present, and no comments were received.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSITIONER YOO to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-23037 RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL THE
  ADOPTION OF AMENDMENTS TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO TITLE 17 TO CONFORM WITH THE CITY'S 2040 GENERAL PLAN
  AND THE REZONING OF CERTAIN PROPERTIES. IN DETERMINING THE CODE
  AMENDMENTS AND PROPERTY REZONINGS ARE EXEMPT FROM THE
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY.

A brief discussion ensued regarding amendments to the motion.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN recommended adding two amendments to the motion, (1)
to request for staff to provide a modification to the proposed ordinance to allow for a conditional
use permit process for a commercial development, to propose either 60 feet in height and or five
stories in height, and (2) the property, located at 26947 Rolling Hills Road (Kelly’s Korner), be

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JUNE 3, 2024
  4
 reconsidered for an alternative land use designation and zoning designation that would allow for
commercial uses only without a mixed-use overlay.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER  agreed  and  amended  the  motion,  seconded  by
COMMISSIONER YOO,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-23037 RECOMMENDING THAT THE CITY COUNCIL
  ADOPT AMENDMENTS TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO TITLE 17 TO CONFORM WITH THE CITY'S 2040 GENERAL PLAN
  AND THE REZONING OF CERTAIN PROPERTIES. IN DETERMINING THE CODE
  AMENDMENTS AND PROPERTY REZONINGS ARE EXEMPT FROM THE
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY. AND (1) TO REQUEST FOR STAFF TO
  PROVIDE A MODIFICATION TO THE PROPOSED ORDINANCE TO ALLOW FOR A
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT PROCESS FOR A COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT, TO
  PROPOSE EITHER 60 FEET IN HEIGHT AND OR FIVE STORIES IN HEIGHT, AND (2)
  THE PROPERTY, LOCATED AT 26947 ROLLING HILLS ROAD (KELLY’S KORNER),
  BE RECONSIDERED FOR AN ALTERNATIVE LAND USE DESIGNATION AND ZONING
  DESIGNATION THAT WOULD ALLOW FOR COMMERCIAL USES ONLY WITHOUT A
  MIXED-USE OVERLAY.

AYES: ROMANELLI, NICKLAS, REPP-LOADMAN, SCHACHTER, YOO
NOES:
ABSENT: MEDAWAR, OLSON
ABSTAIN:

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

NONE

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked for the status of the George F Canyon Nature
Center project. Director Naughton stated that the project is currently out to bid. Administrative
Analyst Corea stated that the bid opening is schedule on June 27 (CORRECTION: June 20).
Director Naughton added that the construction should begin in the fall and will be a 12-18 month
construction period; further updates could be provided at the next meeting. COMMISSIONER
REPP-LOADSMAN commented that the canyon is full of invasives and is under maintained; this
may be an opportunity for the Environmental Advisory Committee to discuss.

CHAIR ROMANELLI asked about the grading activity at 727 Deep Valley Drive. Director
Naughton stated that there were hillside failures due to the heavy rains and that the work that has
been done to the hillside is a result of code enforcement measures in order to ensure the safety
of the tenants on the lower level. Director Naughton stated that the City’s Building Official is in
contact with the property ownership and the crew and it should be another week or two until the
dirt is dried out and ready to be removed.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton thanked the commission for their work on the zoning standards.

CHAIR ROMANELLI thanked staff for their work.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

NONE

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR ROMANELLI adjourned the meeting at 8:17 p.m. to the next regular Planning Commission
meeting on Monday, July 1, 2024 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.
